fitnessSpec.hiking: Strong hiking fitness required — roughly 8-9 miles round trip and ~2,200+ ft of gain to Colchuck Lake, then an additional traverse/scramble above the lake to reach the base, all within a full ~14-16-hour car-to-car day
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light and fast — single rack, rope, and minimal overnight gear if not camping; roughly 20-25 lbs for a single-push day ascent

partner_requirements.approachTime: Roughly 3-4 hours from the Stuart Lake trailhead to the base of the route (Colchuck Lake Trail, then traversing ~400 ft above the lake toward the west face)
requiredSkills: Efficient multi-pitch systems (9 pitches) to keep pace with a ~15-hour day
Rappel competence for the single ~30 m summit rappel, including managing rope-pull issues
Route-finding on featured granite with limited fixed protection
Comfort with remote alpine exposure and self-rescue readiness
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Experienced trad multi-pitch leader comfortable leading sustained 5.10 with a short 5.11+/12- crux; not appropriate for a climber's first alpine multi-pitch outing

fitnessSpec.hiking: Moderate — Spire Gully approach from the SR-20 hairpin
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Light-moderate — full rack for 9 pitches, plus a small aid selection if going the A0 way

partner_requirements.approachTime: ~1–1.5 hours from the SR-20 hairpin pullout to the base of the east buttress
requiredSkills: trad leading 5.9+ crack and face terrain (or 5.11 free if avoiding A0)
basic aid/French-free technique for the A0 sections
rappel descent with rockfall awareness in the gully
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Advanced alpine multi-pitch climber — comfortable either following/leading 5.9 with a short aid move (A0) or leading the 5.11 free variation

fitnessSpec.hiking: Strenuous off-trail alpine approach with sustained steep elevation gain to Boston Basin camp, plus further gain across the Quien Sabe Glacier to the base of the ridge — comparable to a full mountaineering day even before the climbing starts.
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Overnight/multi-day pack (camping gear, rope, rack, glacier travel and crevasse-rescue kit) — moderate-heavy, roughly 30-40 lb, since most parties camp in Boston Basin rather than day-tripping.

partner_requirements.approachTime: Multi-hour approach: steep off-trail hike from the Cascade River Road trailhead to Boston Basin camp (the standard overnight base for this route), then a further glacier crossing to reach the base of the ridge — most parties treat this as a 1-2 night trip rather than a single push. Exact mileage/elevation figures are not recorded.
requiredSkills: Glacier travel and crevasse rescue (crossing the Quien Sabe Glacier is required)
Roped/simul-climbing on moderate (5.4) exposed alpine rock
Comfort with sustained exposure on a knife-edge ridge crest
Judgment around loose rock/loose blocks on ledges
Off-trail routefinding and North Cascades NP wilderness permit logistics
Ability to recognize and retreat from building afternoon thunderstorms
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Intermediate-to-advanced alpine climber: needs prior glacier travel experience and comfort simul-climbing exposed low-5th-class rock while still roped/geared for glacier crossing.
